exercises.title: Improvement cycle 2 — which step?
exercises.problemHtml:
Which step of the cycle is each activity? Assessment can use the troubleshooting guide, questionnaires, interviews; action plans hold at most about ten items, each finishable in 2–3 months; new procedures are piloted on a small scale before roll-out; evaluation checks how the pilots and roll-out went and whether goals were met.

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.

exercises.title: Improvement cycle 3 — the valley of despair
exercises.problemHtml:
Figure 31-7: the learning curve — a short-term productivity drop as people assimilate new ways of working, the "valley of despair". It is part of the investment, not a sign of failure; abandoning the effort in the valley yields a zero return.

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.
exercises.problemHtmlVi:

exercises.title: Improvement cycle 4 — process assets
exercises.problemHtml:
Requirements process assets (Figure 31-8) capture "how we do requirements here": templates (vision and scope, SRS, use case), procedures (elicitation, status tracking, change control), checklists (defect checklist, impact analysis checklist) and examples. Classify each asset.

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.
